proofs.proof_tex:
For a panel law \(P\), Definition \texttt{def:target} gives, at every query
where the displayed conditional expectations exist,
\[
 \tau(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\left\{
 \mathbb E_P[B_{si}(1)\mid z_0]-
 \mathbb E_P[B_{si}(0)\mid z_0]\right\}.                    \tag{1}
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering} gives a common value
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0]=\mu_s(z_0)
 \quad\text{for every replica \(i\)}                         \tag{2}
\]
outside a marginally null set.  The almost-sure equality in
\texttt{ass:consistency} disintegrates to
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{si}(1)\mid z_0]
 =\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0],                \tag{3}
\]
and \texttt{ass:event-date-transport} gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{si}(0)\mid z_0]=m_s(z_{0s}).                 \tag{4}
\]
There are finitely many cohorts and replicas at a fixed triangular-array
index.  Intersecting the conull sets for (2)--(4) and substituting into (1)
proves the panel-law display in the lemma, including its independence of the
replica label.

Now fix an admissible query and a labelled point
\(\xi=(\mathbb K_\xi;\mu,m,\Sigma)\in
\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\).  Equations (2)--(3) in
Definition \texttt{def:fixed-query-kernel-class} give, for every \(i\),
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}=\mu_s,
 \qquad B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}=B_{si}(1)\ \text{almost surely},
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}B_{si}(0)=m_s(z_{0s}).            \tag{5}
\]
Bounded wealth makes all expectations finite.  Hence (5) and
Definition \texttt{def:target} imply
\[
 \tau(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{\mu_s-m_s(z_{0s})\}
 =\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0),                            \tag{6}
\]
where the last equality is Definition
\texttt{def:fixed-query-functional}.  Thus consistency and transport prove
the relationship between the causal target and the observed-law functional;
the relationship is not imposed by definition.  No density, mixing, donor,
rank, inversion, or division condition is used.

Put \(q=Sd\) and
\[
 A=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s},
 \qquad D_X=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\rho_{sX}(z_{0s})^\lambda.    \tag{1}
\]
Every \(n_s\) and \(\pi_s\) is positive, so \(A>0\).  First work in
\(\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)\).  In this experiment \(X,z_0,\Sigma\) are
known specifications; a decision rule may use them but is chosen before the
unknown labelled point \((\mathbb Q_\xi;\mu,f,z)\).

Conditional on the donors define
\[
 U_{si}=E_{si}-\mu_s-K_N^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{K_N}
 \{Q_{s,t_{s\ell},i}-f_s(X_{s,t_{s\ell}})\}.                \tag{2}
\]
Donor--history independence and independence of histories across \((s,i)\)
make these variables conditionally centered and independent across
\((s,i)\).  Boundedness gives \(|U_{si}|\le4B\), and therefore
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb Q_\xi}\!\left(
 \sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}U_{si}
 \mathrel{\Big|}(Z_j)_j\right)\le16B^2A.                    \tag{3}
\]
Let \(t_s^0\) be the smallest nearest design index to \(z_{0s}\).  By the
definition of \(t_{s\ell}\) and two triangle inequalities,
\[
 \|X_{s,t_{s\ell}}-z_s\|_2
 \le\rho_{sX}(z_{0s})+\|z_s-z_{0s}\|_2
       +2\|\widetilde z_{\ell s}-z_s\|_2.                  \tag{4}
\]
Subadditivity of \(x^\lambda\) and Holder continuity imply
\[
 |f_s(X_{s,t_{s\ell}})-f_s(z_s)|
 \le C\{\rho_{sX}(z_{0s})^\lambda+
 \|z_s-z_{0s}\|_2^\lambda+
 \|\widetilde z_{\ell s}-z_s\|_2^\lambda\}.              \tag{5}
\]
Projection onto the cube is nonexpansive, each balanced fold has size at
least \(N/3\), and \(\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma)\le qC_\Sigma\).  Hence
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}\|\widetilde z_\ell-z\|_2^2
 \le\frac{\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma)}{|I_\ell|}
 \le\frac{3qC_\Sigma}{N}.                                   \tag{6}
\]
The experiment also imposes \(\|z-z_0\|_2^2\le C_\Sigma/N\).  Expanding
\(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{opt}}-\theta_{\mathfrak E}(\xi)\) into the
centered sum in (3) and the approximation errors in (5), applying Jensen's
inequality to (6), and using \((x+y+z)^2\le3(x^2+y^2+z^2)\), gives
\[
 \sup_{\xi\in\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}
 \{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{opt}}-\theta_{\mathfrak E}(\xi)\}^2
 \le C\{A+D_X^2+N^{-\lambda}\}.                            \tag{7}
\]
The estimator is measurable in the observations and known specifications
and does not use \((\mu,f,z)\); it is therefore an admissible minimax
witness.  Under \(\delta_0<1/2\), Lemma
\texttt{lem:rough-holder-optimal-recovery-geometry} makes the right side at
most \(CR_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\).

For later lower bounds, suppose two laws \(P_0,P_1\) have target separation
\(\Delta\) and total variation at most \(1-\eta\).  For
\(A_0=\{|\widetilde\theta-\theta_0|<\Delta/2\}\), the triangle inequality
shows that the squared error is at least \(\Delta^2/4\) under law one on
\(A_0\), and under law zero on \(A_0^c\).  Consequently
\[
 \max_{v=0,1}\mathbb E_v(\widetilde\theta-\theta_v)^2
 \ge\frac{\Delta^2}{8}\{P_0(A_0^c)+P_1(A_0)\}
 \ge\frac{\eta\Delta^2}{8}.                                 \tag{8}
\]

For the treated-mean channel take \(f_s=0\), \(Q_{sti}=0\), \(z=z_0\),
and fix the donor law.  Under \(v\in\{-1,1\}\), let the \(E_{si}\)'s be
independent with values \(\{-b,b\}\), where \(0<b<B\), and
\[
 \Pr_v(E_{si}=b)=\frac12+v\varepsilon_s,
 \qquad \varepsilon_s=\frac{\gamma\pi_s}{bn_s\sqrt A}.      \tag{9}
\]
Because \(A\ge\pi_s^2/n_s\), sufficiently small fixed \(\gamma\) puts all
probabilities in \([1/4,3/4]\).  The target separation is
\(4\gamma\sqrt A\), and the Hellinger affinity is
\[
 \prod_{s=1}^{S}(1-4\varepsilon_s^2)^{n_s/2}
 \ge \exp(-C\gamma^2/b^2)>0,                                \tag{10}
\]
since \(\sum_sn_s\varepsilon_s^2=\gamma^2/b^2\).  The
Cauchy--Schwarz affinity bound used in
\texttt{lem:full-covariance-location-pair} keeps total variation below one,
so (8) gives risk at least \(cA\).  The zero-displacement member of that
lemma supplies a donor law with the prescribed covariance; strict
fourth-moment slack guarantees membership.

For the fixed-design channel put
\[
 q_s(x)=a_0\min_{1\le t\le T}\|x-X_{st}\|_2^\lambda,
 \qquad f_s=q_s/2,\quad g_s=-q_s/2,                           \tag{11}
\]
with \(a_0\) small.  Lemma
\texttt{lem:rough-holder-optimal-recovery-geometry} verifies that these
surfaces are admissible and coincide at all design sites.  Deterministic
zero responses, identical event laws, and identical donors therefore yield
identical observations, while the targets differ by \(a_0D_X\).  Equation
(8) with \(\eta=1\) yields risk at least \(cD_X^2\).

For the donor channel apply Lemma
\texttt{lem:full-covariance-location-pair}, choosing the displaced coordinate
in cohort \(s_0\).  Under both alternatives use the common surface
\[
 f_{s_0}(x)=a_1|x_k-z_{0,s_0k}|^\lambda,
 \qquad f_s(x)=0\quad(s\ne s_0),                             \tag{12}
\]
with \(a_1\) small enough for the Holder and support restrictions, and keep
the response and event laws identical.  If \(e\) is the displaced
coordinate, that lemma and ellipticity give
\[
 |z_{1,e}-z_{0,e}|
 =\frac{c_\eta N^{-1/2}}{\|\Sigma^{-1/2}e\|_2}
 \ge c_\eta c_\Sigma^{1/2}N^{-1/2}.                         \tag{13}
\]
The donor products have total variation at most \(1-\eta\), while (12)--(13)
separate targets by at least \(cN^{-\lambda/2}\).  Equation (8) gives risk
at least \(cN^{-\lambda}\).  The maximum of the three lower bounds and the
two-sided characterization in the rough-geometry lemma prove
\[
 \inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_{\xi\in\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}
 \{\widetilde\tau-\theta_{\mathfrak E}(\xi)\}^2
 \ge cR_{X,\mathrm{opt}}.                                   \tag{14}
\]

Now fix \(\xi=(\mathbb K_\xi;\mu,m,\Sigma)\in
\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\).  Definition
\texttt{def:fixed-query-kernel-class} gives, conditionally on the exact
design, donor--panel independence, independence of histories across
\((s,i)\), and
\[
 \mathbb E[Q_{sti}\mid\mathcal X]=m_s(X_{st}),
 \qquad
 \mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathcal X]=\mu_s.      \tag{15}
\]
Thus for almost every design the conditional observed law, with its labels,
is the central point \(z=z_0\) of \(\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)\).  Bounded
responses give \(|m_s(X_{st})|\le B\) almost surely; the lower design-density
bound makes this true Lebesgue-almost everywhere, and Holder continuity
extends it to all \(x\).  Hence \(\|m_s\|_\infty\le B\), as required by the
experiment.  Its target is
\[
 \theta_{\mathfrak E}
 =\sum_s\pi_s\{\mu_s-m_s(z_{0s})\}
 =\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0).                            \tag{16}
\]
Applying (7) conditionally proves the nearest-design bound.  If every cohort
design contains \(z_{0s}\), then \(D_X=0\), and the exact-site risk and
modulus conclusions follow from (7) and the rough-geometry lemma.

Suppose instead \(g_{sT}(z_0)<1\) for every \(s\).  Then
\((z_{0s},h_s^\star)\) is feasible in every foldwise anchor search, and
certificate optimality gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &C_H\|\widehat u_{s\ell}-\widetilde z_{\ell s}\|_2^\lambda
 +C_H\widehat h_{s\ell}^\lambda
 +C_V(Tn_s\widehat h_{s\ell}^d)^{-1/2}\\
 &\quad\le C_H\|z_{0s}-\widetilde z_{\ell s}\|_2^\lambda
 +C_H(h_s^\star)^\lambda
 +C_V\{Tn_s(h_s^\star)^d\}^{-1/2}.
 \end{aligned}                                               \tag{17}
\]
The bandwidth floor bounds the last term by a constant multiple of
\((h_s^\star)^\lambda\).  Since \(r=0\), Gram coercivity makes every fit
invertible and its intercept weights nonnegative with sum one; clipping is
therefore inactive for responses in \([-B,B]\).  Holder continuity bounds
approximation bias by the first two terms on the left of (17), while (15)
and whole-history independence give centered variance at most \(CA\).
Donor unbiasedness, projection contraction, and ellipticity give
\[
 \mathbb E\|\widetilde z_\ell-z_0\|_2^2\le3qC_\Sigma/N.     \tag{18}
\]
Jensen's inequality and (17)--(18) now yield
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 [\{\widehat\tau-\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)\}^2
 \mid(X_{st})]\le CR_D.                                    \tag{19}
\]
The rough-geometry lemma also gives \(R_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\le CR_D\).

Finally let \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\).  The corrected Lemma
\texttt{lem:panel-fixed-query-kernel-transfer} supplies, for
marginal-almost-every admissible query, the labelled point
\[
 \xi_P(z_0)=\bigl(\mathbb K_{P,z_0};\mu_P(z_0),m,
                         \Sigma_P(z_0)\bigr)
 \in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0),                         \tag{20}
\]
not membership of the bare kernel.  Lemma
\texttt{lem:causal-identification} gives
\(\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi_P(z_0);z_0)=\tau(z_0)\) on the same conull set.
Equations (16)--(19) therefore transfer to the causal conditional problem at
those query values and at conditional-almost-every design.  The deterministic
subexperiment permits dependence on known \(X,z_0,\Sigma\), whereas the
feasible outer estimators are observable-data rules and do not receive the
unknown query.  No conditional version is selected at a query-null value.

Write
\[
 A=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s},
 \qquad D_T=\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right\}^{2\lambda/d}. \tag{1}
\]
Fix \(z_0\in\mathcal Z_{\delta_0}\) and a labelled point
\(\xi\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\).  The estimator in
\texttt{def:frontier-estimator} is one \(\mathcal O\)-measurable rule built
from the donor sample and observed panel.  It receives neither \(z_0\) nor
a nuisance label, so it is selected before both outer suprema.

Let \(\mathcal G=\{g_{sT}(z_0)<1\text{ for every }s\}\).  On
\(\mathcal G\), Theorem \texttt{thm:conditional-frontier} bounds conditional
risk by \(CR_D\).  The estimator and target lie in \([-2B,2B]\), so squared
error is at most \(16B^2\) on \(\mathcal G^c\).  Because
\(0<h_s^\star\le1\),
\[
 \Pr(\mathcal G^c)\le\sum_s\Pr(h_s^\star=1)
 \le\sum_s\mathbb E(h_s^\star)^{2\lambda}.                  \tag{2}
\]
The bandwidth floor gives
\[
 \{Tn_s(h_s^\star)^d\}^{-1/2}\le(h_s^\star)^\lambda.       \tag{3}
\]
Apply Lemma \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-anchor-moment} to (2)--(3), and use
Cauchy--Schwarz and Minkowski on the weighted bandwidth sum.  Uniformly over
the fixed query and labelled point,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 [\{\widehat\tau-\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)\}^2]
 \le C\bigg[&A+
 \left\{\sum_s\pi_s(Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}\right\}^2\\
 &+D_T+N^{-\lambda}\bigg]
 \le CR_\star.
 \end{aligned}                                               \tag{4}
\]
Only design mixing enters the occupancy bound; centered sampling is over
complete independent unit histories.

The smoothing term is redundant.  With \(a_s=n_s^{-1/2}\) and
\(b=T^{-\lambda/d}\), exponent arithmetic gives
\[
 (Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}
 =a_s^{2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}b^{d/(2\lambda+d)}
 \le a_s\vee b.                                               \tag{5}
\]
Since \(S\) is fixed, Cauchy--Schwarz yields
\[
 \left\{\sum_s\pi_s(Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}\right\}^2
 \le C\{A+T^{-2\lambda/d}\}\le C(A+D_T).                  \tag{6}
\]

For the converse, the two-point argument (8) in the proof of
\texttt{thm:conditional-frontier} says that separation \(\Delta\) and total
variation at most \(1-\eta\) imply squared risk at least
\(\eta\Delta^2/8\).  At \(z_0=\tfrac12\mathbf1\), embed the treated pair
from that proof with an i.i.d. uniform design, constant untreated regression,
and common admissible donors.  Its treated conditional mean is common within
each cohort and its target separation is \(4\gamma\sqrt A\); its product
Hellinger affinity is bounded away from zero.  It therefore gives a lower
bound \(cA\).

Lemma \texttt{lem:donor-location-two-point-family} supplies two labelled
points at different admissible queries with target separation
\(cN^{-\lambda/2}\) and total variation bounded away from one.  Because the
outer infimum selects one observable rule before the query, this yields
\(cN^{-\lambda}\).  Lemma
\texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-cluster-two-point-family} supplies two points in
one fixed-query class with common mass bounded away from zero and separation
of order \(D_T^{1/2}\), yielding \(cD_T\).  Combining the three lower bounds
with (6) proves
\[
 \inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_{z_0\in\mathcal Z_{\delta_0}}
 \sup_{\xi\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 [\{\widetilde\tau-\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)\}^2]
 \asymp A\vee D_T\vee N^{-\lambda}\asymp R_\star.          \tag{7}
\]

On the independent-calendar subclass, the anchor lemma replaces \(D_T\) in
the upper bound by \(T^{-2\lambda/d}\).  For the reverse inequality use an
i.i.d. uniform design and a cube of radius \(r_T=cT^{-1/d}\) around
\(z_{01}\).  Compare a constant surface to that surface plus
\(ar_T^\lambda\phi((x-z_{01})/r_T)\), where \(\phi\) is a fixed smooth bump
supported in the cube and \(a>0\) is small.  These surfaces satisfy the
Holder and support bounds.  For sufficiently small fixed \(c\),
\[
 \Pr\{X_{1t}\text{ misses the cube for all }t\}
 \ge(1-v_dr_T^d)^T\ge c_2>0.                                \tag{8}
\]
On this event the two observed laws coincide, while the targets differ by
\(c_1T^{-\lambda/d}\).  The two-point inequality gives the lower squared-risk
term \(cT^{-2\lambda/d}\).

When \(S=1\), \(H=0\), \(p=d=1\), and \(n_1=n\), (4) has the bookkeeping
scale
\[
 n^{-1}\vee(Tn)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+1)}
 \vee T^{-2\lambda}\vee N^{-\lambda}.
\]
Equation (6) proves that its smoothing term is dominated by the maximum of
the first and third terms.  Finally, the corrected transfer lemma gives the
labelled point \(\xi_P(z_0)\) for marginal-almost-every query of each panel
law, and Lemma \texttt{lem:causal-identification} gives
\(\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi_P(z_0);z_0)=\tau(z_0)\).  Applying (4) on that
conull set proves the causal transfer without assigning class membership to
a bare kernel or evaluating a null conditional version.

Fix \(z_0\in\mathcal Z_{\delta_0}\) and
\(\xi=(\mathbb K_\xi;\mu,m,\Sigma)\in
\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\).  Boundedness gives
\(\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)\in[-2B,2B]\).  On the regular branch,
\(r=0\), and selected Gram coercivity makes each local-constant fit
invertible.  Its weights are nonnegative and sum to one; since response
averages lie in \([-B,B]\), clipping is inactive.  Conditional on the exact
design and donors, the selected weights are response-independent.  Define
one variable per complete unit history by
\[
 \zeta_{si}=\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}\left[
 B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_s-
 \sum_{t=1}^{T}w_{st}\{Q_{sti}-m_s(X_{st})\}\right].          \tag{1}
\]
Donor--panel independence and the two mean equalities in
\texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering} center (1).  Conditional
cross-unit independence makes the variables independent across \((s,i)\);
no within-history independence is used.  Their range lengths are at most
\[
 d_{si}=\frac{2B\pi_s}{n_s}
 \left(1+\sum_{t=1}^{T}|w_{st}|\right).                      \tag{2}
\]
For \(V\in[a,b]\), convexity of the exponential gives
\(\mathbb E e^{u(V-\mathbb EV)}\le e^{u^2(b-a)^2/8}\).
Multiplying this inequality over histories, applying exponential Markov to
both tails, and optimizing over \(u>0\) shows
\[
 \Pr_{\mathbb K_\xi}\left\{
 \left|\sum_{s,i}\zeta_{si}\right|>r_{\mathrm{unit}}
 \mathrel{\Big|}\mathcal X,(Z_j)_j\right\}
 \le\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}.                                   \tag{3}
\]
Indeed, \(\sum_{s,i}d_{si}^2=4B^2A_w\), and the displayed
\(r_{\mathrm{unit}}\) in \texttt{def:honest-interval} exceeds the resulting
Hoeffding radius; its positive linear term only enlarges it.

Put \(q=Sd\).  Spectral clipping gives
\(\widehat\Sigma\succeq(c_\Sigma/2)I_q\).  Each donor fold has size at least
\(N/3\), so donor unbiasedness and \(\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I_q\) imply
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}\left[
 N\|\widehat\Sigma^{-1/2}(\overline Z_\ell-z_0)\|_2^2\right]
 \le\frac{6qC_\Sigma}{c_\Sigma}.                             \tag{4}
\]
This needs no independence between the sample mean and sample covariance.
Markov's inequality, a union bound over at most two folds, and the definition
of \(q_{\mathrm{don}}\) give
\[
 \Pr\left\{\max_\ell\|\widehat\Sigma^{-1/2}
 (\overline Z_\ell-z_0)\|_2>q_{\mathrm{don}}N^{-1/2}\right\}
 \le\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}.                                  \tag{5}
\]
On its complement, \(\widehat\Sigma\preceq2C_\Sigma I_q\), and projection
onto the cube is nonexpansive relative to \(z_0\), whence
\[
 \max_\ell\|\widetilde z_\ell-z_0\|_2
 \le(2C_\Sigma)^{1/2}q_{\mathrm{don}}N^{-1/2}.               \tag{6}
\]

At a selected local-constant fit, nonnegative unit-mass weights and kernel
support imply
\[
 \left|\sum_tw_{st}^{(\ell)}m_s(X_{st})
       -m_s(\widetilde z_{\ell s})\right|
 \le C\{\|\widehat u_{s\ell}-\widetilde z_{\ell s}\|_2^\lambda
          +\widehat h_{s\ell}^\lambda\}.                    \tag{7}
\]
Holder continuity from \(\widetilde z_{\ell s}\) to \(z_{0s}\), (6), and the
calibration of \(C_H\) bound total deterministic error by
\(r_{\mathrm{bias}}+r_{\mathrm{don}}\).  Equations (3), (5), and
\(\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}+\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}=\alpha\) prove coverage on the
regular branch.  Every declared bad branch returns \([-2B,2B]\), which
contains the target; intersecting a covering interval with this known range
preserves coverage.  This proves the stated uniform asymptotic coverage.

For expected length, \(\sum_t|w_{st}|=1\) on the regular branch.  Thus, with
\(A=\sum_s\pi_s^2/n_s\),
\[
 r_{\mathrm{samp}}\le C(\alpha,B)A^{1/2},                    \tag{8}
\]
where \(\max_s\pi_s/n_s\le A^{1/2}\).  Let
\(\mathcal G=\{h_s^\star<1\text{ for every }s\}\).  On \(\mathcal G\),
certificate optimality at \((z_{0s},h_s^\star)\) and the bandwidth floor
give
\[
 r_{\mathrm{bias}}\le C\sum_s\pi_s\left\{(h_s^\star)^\lambda+
 K_N^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{K_N}
 \|\widetilde z_\ell-z_0\|_2^\lambda\right\}.                \tag{9}
\]
Donor unbiasedness, ellipticity, projection contraction, and Jensen give
\[
 \mathbb E\|\widetilde z_\ell-z_0\|_2^\lambda
 \le CN^{-\lambda/2}.                                       \tag{10}
\]
The interval length is at most \(4B\), and
\[
 \Pr(\mathcal G^c)\le\sum_s\mathbb E(h_s^\star)^{2\lambda}.  \tag{11}
\]
Using Lemma \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-anchor-moment} in (9)--(11) yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E\operatorname{length}(C_\alpha)
 \le C\bigg[&A^{1/2}+
 \sum_s\pi_s(Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}
 +\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right\}^{\lambda/d}
 +N^{-\lambda/2}\bigg]+CR_\star.
 \end{aligned}                                               \tag{12}
\]
All searches are finite or compact with deterministic fallbacks, and
spectral clipping is total.  Along the stated growth arrays the small-sample
fallbacks disappear.  The smoothing domination in
\texttt{thm:marginal-phase-diagram}, and \(R_\star\le R_\star^{1/2}\) for all
sufficiently large indices, turn (12) into
\[
 \sup_{z_0}\sup_\xi
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}\operatorname{length}(C_\alpha)
 \le CR_\star^{1/2}.                                        \tag{13}
\]
In the independent-calendar subclass, the anchor lemma replaces the
logarithmic length term by \(T^{-\lambda/d}\).

For the converse, suppose two observed laws with targets
\(\theta_0,\theta_1\) possess a common subprobability measure \(\nu\) of mass
\(\eta>2\alpha\).  Uniform coverage \(1-\alpha-o(1)\) under both gives
\[
 \nu\{\theta_0,\theta_1\in I_\alpha\}\ge\eta-2\alpha-o(1).   \tag{14}
\]
Every interval on this event has length at least
\(|\theta_1-\theta_0|\), so
\[
 \max_{v=0,1}\mathbb E_v\operatorname{length}(I_\alpha)
 \ge|\theta_1-\theta_0|\{\eta-2\alpha-o(1)\}.                \tag{15}
\]
For arbitrary \(P_0,P_1\), this common measure is obtained by taking
\(\vartheta=P_0+P_1\) and
\[
 d\nu=\min\{dP_0/d\vartheta,dP_1/d\vartheta\}\,d\vartheta;
\]
its mass is \(1-\|P_1-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\).

The treated pair in the marginal proof has common cohort means and overlap
arbitrarily close to one after reducing \(\gamma\); (15) yields
\(cA^{1/2}\).  For the donor channel apply
\texttt{lem:full-covariance-location-pair} with \(\eta\in(2\alpha,1)\).
Use a common independent uniform design and, in the displaced cohort, the
common regression
\[
 m(x)=b_0+a_0|x_k-z_k^{(0)}|^\lambda,                        \tag{16}
\]
with constant regressions elsewhere, deterministic responses
\(Q_{sti}=m_s(X_{st})\), a common positive treated wealth, and untreated
event wealth \(m_s(z_s^{(v)})\) under alternative \(v\).  Small
\(a_0,b_0\) verify support and Holder smoothness.  The panel coordinates
coincide, the donor laws have common mass at least \(\eta\), and ellipticity
converts the Mahalanobis displacement into coordinate separation at least
\(cN^{-1/2}\).  Thus (16) separates targets by
\(cN^{-\lambda/2}\), and (15) gives that length lower bound.

Lemma \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-cluster-two-point-family} supplies common
mass exceeding \(2\alpha\) and target separation
\(c\{\log(T\vee2)/T\}^{\lambda/d}\).  Equation (15), followed by smoothing
domination, gives \(cR_\star^{1/2}\).  In the independent-calendar class,
the no-hit cube from the marginal proof may be chosen with common mass
exceeding \(2\alpha\), giving \(cT^{-\lambda/d}\).  These pairs prove the
converse for every one \(\mathcal O\)-measurable interval chosen before the
unknown query and label.

Finally, the corrected transfer lemma supplies the labelled point
\(\xi_P(z_0)\) for marginal-almost-every query of each panel law, and
\texttt{lem:causal-identification} gives
\(\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi_P(z_0);z_0)=\tau(z_0)\).  Applying (3)--(13) on
that conull set proves the causal coverage and length upper conclusions.
No membership is attributed to a bare conditional law and nothing is
asserted at a query-null version.

Fix \(z_0\) and
\(\xi=(\mathbb K_\xi;\mu,m,\Sigma)\in
\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\).  Boundedness makes all following
expectations finite, and design centering gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 [B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_s\mid\mathcal X]=0.              \tag{1}
\]
For bounded \(\mathcal X\)-measurable \(W\), the pull-out and tower
properties imply
\[
 \mathbb E[(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_s)W]
 =\mathbb E\!\left[W\,
   \mathbb E(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_s\mid\mathcal X)\right]=0. \tag{2}
\]
Taking \(W=\mathbf1_E\) gives
\(\mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mathbf1_E]=\mu_s\mathbb K_\xi(E)\).
Division by \(\mathbb K_\xi(E)>0\), and the analogous argument for \(E^c\)
when \(\mathbb K_\xi(E)<1\), prove that both conditional means equal
\(\mu_s\).  Lemma \texttt{lem:common-design-shock-obstruction} then gives
the stated exclusion.  By the corrected Lemma
\texttt{lem:panel-fixed-query-kernel-transfer}, the same argument applies to
the labelled point \(\xi_P(z_0)\), rather than to its bare kernel, for
marginal-almost-every query of every panel law.

It remains to construct the variance certificate.  For arbitrary positive
\(N,T,n_1\), take
\[
 S=1,\quad\pi_1=1,\quad H=0,\quad p=d=1,\quad z_0=\tfrac12,
 \quad\lambda=\kappa=1,\quad B=L=1,\quad\delta_0=\tfrac14,  \tag{3}
\]
and \(c_X=C_X=c_\Sigma=C_\Sigma=1\).  Let
\((X_{1t})_t\), \((\eta_j)_j\), and \((\varepsilon_i)_i\) be mutually
independent, with \(X_{1t}\) i.i.d. uniform on \([0,1]\) and \(\eta_j\),
\(\varepsilon_i\) i.i.d. Rademacher.  Define
\[
 m_1(x)=\tfrac12,\qquad Q_{1ti}=\tfrac12,
 \qquad Z_j=\tfrac12+\eta_j.                                 \tag{4}
\]
Set \(W_{1i,-1}=1/2\), \(R_{1i0}(0)=0\), and therefore
\(B_{1i}(0)=1/2\).  Under \(\mathbb K_0\), set \(R_{1i0}(1)=0\); under
\(\mathbb K_1\), set \(R_{1i0}(1)=\varepsilon_i/2\).  Consistency gives
\[
 B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}=\tfrac12\quad(\mathbb K_0),
 \qquad
 B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}=\tfrac12+\tfrac14\varepsilon_i
 \quad(\mathbb K_1).                                        \tag{5}
\]
The smallest return is \(-1/2>-1\), so the return support is respected.

Give both kernels labels \(\mu_1=1/2\), \(m_1\) from (4), and
\(\Sigma=1\).  Wealth is bounded by one, the constant regression lies in
\(\mathcal H_1(1,1)\), and \(z_0\) is interior.  The uniform design has
density one and beta-mixing coefficients zero.  Conditional on
\(\mathcal X\), histories are independent across \(i\), and
\[
 \mathbb E[Q_{1ti}\mid\mathcal X]=\tfrac12=m_1(X_{1t}),
 \qquad
 \mathbb E[B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathcal X]
 =\mathbb E B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}=\tfrac12=\mu_1.            \tag{6}
\]
Thus the treated mean is common across replicas; no identical-distribution
or within-history independence premise is used.  Donors are independent of
the panel and satisfy
\[
 \mathbb EZ_j=z_0,
 \qquad\operatorname{Var}(Z_j)=1,
 \qquad\mathbb E|Z_j-z_0|^4=1=B^4.                           \tag{7}
\]
Finally, \(\mathbb EB_{1i}(0)=1/2=m_1(z_0)\), so transport holds.  Equations
(3)--(7) verify every clause of the fixed-query class, giving labelled points
\(\xi^{(0)},\xi^{(1)}\).  Taking the query identically \(1/2\) yields panel
laws \(P^{(0)},P^{(1)}\) satisfying the panel class without invoking a null
conditional version.

The joint law of \(((X_{1t})_t,(Q_{1ti})_{t,i},(Z_j)_j)\) is common to the
two kernels.  Definition \texttt{def:target}, (5), and
\(\mathbb E\varepsilon_i=0\) give \(\tau(z_0)=0\) under both.  Nevertheless,
independence of \(\varepsilon_i\) from \(\mathcal X\) gives
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb K_0}(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathcal X)=0,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb K_1}(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathcal X)
 =\tfrac1{16}.                                                \tag{8}
\]
This is the required explicit certificate: centering removes the obsolete
common-design shock but does not determine the remaining event-noise
constant.

Put \(p_E=\mathbb K_\xi(E)\).  Bounded wealth and consistency imply
\(|B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}|\le B\), so all expectations below exist.  Since
\(E\in\mathcal X\) and \(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}=b\mathbf1_E\),
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathcal X]
 =b\mathbf1_E.                                                \tag{1}
\]
The design-centering clause of
\texttt{def:fixed-query-kernel-class} gives instead
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathcal X]
 =\mu_s,                                                       \tag{2}
\]
where \(\mu_s=\mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\).  Taking
expectations in the shock representation gives \(\mu_s=bp_E\).  Therefore
(1)--(2), followed by squaring and integration, imply
\[
 0=\mathbb E[(b\mathbf1_E-bp_E)^2]=b^2p_E(1-p_E).            \tag{3}
\]
Since \(b\ne0\), division by \(b^2>0\) and \(p_E\in[0,1]\) give
\(p_E\in\{0,1\}\).  In the scalar law described in the statement,
\(X_{11}\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\) and \(q\in(0,1)\), so
\(p_E=\Pr(X_{11}\le q)=q\in(0,1)\), contradicting (3).  Hence that law is
not in the fixed-query class.  No transport, temporal-mixing, or donor
condition is used.

Put \(q=Sd\) and \(\Delta_B=B^4-q^2>0\).  Choose \(a_D>1\) with
\(a_D^2<1+\Delta_B/2\).  For \(|u|\) sufficiently small define
\(V_u\in\{-a_D,0,a_D\}\) by
\[
 p_+(u)=\frac{1+u^2}{2a_D^2}+\frac{u}{2a_D},\quad
 p_-(u)=\frac{1+u^2}{2a_D^2}-\frac{u}{2a_D},\quad
 p_0(u)=1-\frac{1+u^2}{a_D^2}.                               \tag{1}
\]
These are positive probabilities near zero, and direct summation gives
\(\mathbb EV_u=u\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(V_u)=1\).  Adjoin independent
Rademacher variables \(R_2,\ldots,R_q\).  At \(u=0\),
\[
 \mathbb E\|(V_0,R_2,\ldots,R_q)\|_2^4
 =a_D^2+2(q-1)+(q-1)^2=q^2-1+a_D^2<B^4.                     \tag{2}
\]
The centered fourth moment is continuous in \(u\), so the strict inequality
persists on a smaller fixed neighborhood.

Let \(z^{(0)}=\tfrac12\mathbf1_q\),
\(z^{(1)}=z^{(0)}+\delta_Ne_1\), and \(\delta_N=c_*N^{-1/2}\).  Under
alternative \(v\), let donors have first coordinate
\(1/2+V_{v\delta_N}\) and all remaining coordinates \(1/2+R_k\).  Then
\[
 \mathbb E_vZ_j=z^{(v)},\qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_v(Z_j)=I_q,\qquad
 \mathbb E_v\|Z_j-z^{(v)}\|_2^4\le B^4.                    \tag{3}
\]
The covariance is admissible because \(c_\Sigma\le1\le C_\Sigma\), and
strict interior slack keeps both queries admissible for large \(N\).

The square roots of the probabilities in (1) have bounded second
derivatives near zero.  Their affinity equals one at zero and has derivative
\(\tfrac12\sum_rp_r'(0)=0\); hence the one-donor Hellinger affinity is at
least \(1-C_0\delta_N^2\).  Product factorization and the affinity--total
variation inequality proved in
\texttt{lem:full-covariance-location-pair} give
\[
 \|P_1^{Z,N}-P_0^{Z,N}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le\{1-(1-C_0\delta_N^2)^{2N}\}^{1/2}.                    \tag{4}
\]
Choosing fixed \(c_*>0\) small makes (4) at most \(1-\eta_0\).

Use a common i.i.d. uniform exact design.  If \(0<\lambda<1\), so
\(\kappa=\lambda\), set
\[
 m_1(x)=b_0+b_1(x_1-1/2)_+^\kappa;
\]
if \(\lambda\ge1\), so \(\kappa=1\), set
\(m_1(x)=b_0+b_1(x_1-1/2)\); set every other surface to \(b_0\).
Subadditivity of the \(\kappa\)-power in the first case and the fact that an
affine function has vanishing derivatives above order one in the second show
that sufficiently small positive \(b_0,b_1\) put every surface in
\(\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\) and inside the wealth bound.  The common surface
satisfies
\[
 |m_1(z_1^{(1)})-m_1(z_1^{(0)})|=b_1\delta_N^\kappa.         \tag{5}
\]
Take deterministic training responses \(Q_{sti}=m_s(X_{st})\) and the same
positive constant treated observation for every cohort and replica under
both laws.  Set \(B_{si}(1)=B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) and
\(B_{si}(0)=m_s(z_s^{(v)})\).  With baseline wealth one, horizon-zero return
equal to wealth minus one, and later returns zero, these levels satisfy
\texttt{def:buyhold-level}; small positive \(b_0,b_1\) keep every return
above \(-1\).  Conditional centering, common treated-mean replication,
cross-unit independence, consistency, and transport are then exact.  The
uniform design has density one and zero beta-mixing coefficients, and donors
are independent of the common panel.  Thus both constructed laws belong to
\(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\).

All observed panel coordinates have the same law; only the donor-location
factor differs.  Lemma \texttt{lem:causal-identification} and (5) give
\[
 |\tau_1(z^{(1)})-\tau_0(z^{(0)})|
 =\pi_1b_1c_*^\kappa N^{-\kappa/2}.                          \tag{6}
\]
Equations (3)--(6) prove the stated root-\(N\) query separation, overlap,
and target modulus without a class-wide lower-modulus assumption.

Put \(q=Sd\) and choose the common realized path
\(z_0=\tfrac12\mathbf1_q\), which is admissible because
\(\delta_0\le1/2\).  Since \(B^4\ge q^2\), the common donor law
\(Z_j=z_0+U_j\), with independent Rademacher coordinates in \(U_j\), has
mean \(z_0\), covariance \(I_q\), and fourth standardized norm moment
\(q^2\).  Take it independent of the panel.  Choose \(\gamma>0\) with
\(e^{-\gamma}>2\alpha\), and set
\[
 L_T=\left\lfloor
 \frac{\log T-2\log\log(T\vee3)}{|\log\rho_0|}
 \right\rfloor\vee1,
 \qquad p_T=\frac{\gamma L_T}{T}.                            \tag{1}
\]
For all large \(T\),
\[
 2p_T\le\beta_0\rho_0^{L_T-1}.                              \tag{2}
\]

Partition the first cohort's calendar into complete consecutive blocks of
length \(L_T\).  Independently label each complete block by
\(C_b\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_T)\).  Let \(A_T\) be a cube centered
at \(z_{01}=\tfrac12\mathbf1_d\) with volume \(p_T\).  Conditional on
\(C_b=1\), draw the block's design points independently uniformly on
\(A_T\); conditional on \(C_b=0\), draw them independently uniformly on
\(A_T^c\).  Every complete-block date then has density
\[
 p_T\frac{\mathbf1_{A_T}(x)}{p_T}
 +(1-p_T)\frac{\mathbf1_{A_T^c}(x)}{1-p_T}=1                \tag{3}
\]
Lebesgue-almost everywhere.  Draw the incomplete block and all other cohorts
independently uniformly.

At lag \(k<L_T\), the separated past and future sigma-fields share at most
one block label.  Replacing that future-side label by an independent copy
couples the fields at mismatch probability
\(2p_T(1-p_T)\le2p_T\); at \(k\ge L_T\), the fields use disjoint labels and
are independent.  Since \(\rho_0^k\ge\rho_0^{L_T-1}\) for \(k<L_T\), (2)
gives
\[
 \beta(k)\le\beta_0\rho_0^k.                                \tag{4}
\]

Let \(E_T\) be the event that every complete-block label is zero and that no
point in the incomplete block lies in a fixed smaller concentric cube.  The
incomplete-block failure probability is at most \(L_Tp_T=o(1)\), while
\[
 \Pr(E_T)=(1-p_T)^{\lfloor T/L_T\rfloor}-o(1)
 \longrightarrow e^{-\gamma}>
 \eta_\alpha:=\frac{e^{-\gamma}+2\alpha}{2}>2\alpha.        \tag{5}
\]
Let \(h_T\asymp p_T^{1/d}\) be the side scale of that smaller cube.  Choose
a fixed smooth bump \(\phi\), supported in the unit cube and satisfying
\(\phi(0)=1\).  For sufficiently small fixed \(a,b_0>0\), put
\[
 m_{10}(x)=b_0,\qquad
 m_{11}(x)=b_0+ah_T^\lambda
                 \phi((x-z_{01})/h_T),                      \tag{6}
\]
and keep all other surfaces equal to \(b_0\).  A derivative of order
\(j\le\lfloor\lambda\rfloor\) is bounded by a constant times
\(h_T^{\lambda-j}\), and the top derivative has uniformly bounded Holder
seminorm.  Thus (6) belongs to \(\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\), and the chosen
constants enforce boundedness.

Under alternative \(v\), set \(Q_{1ti}=m_{1v}(X_{1t})\), use the common
constant surfaces elsewhere, and use the same positive constant treated
observation for every replica.  Set treated potential wealth equal to that
observation and untreated event wealth to \(m_{sv}(z_{0s})\).  Baseline one,
horizon-zero return wealth minus one, and later returns zero realize these
levels.  All centering, common-mean, independence, consistency, transport,
support, density, mixing, and donor clauses have now been verified, so the
two laws lie in the panel class and induce labelled points in one fixed-query
class.

On \(E_T\), no response is evaluated in the bump support.  The restrictions
of the two observed laws to \(E_T\) therefore coincide and define a common
subprobability measure of mass at least \(\eta_\alpha\) for large \(T\).
Lemma \texttt{lem:causal-identification}, (1), and (6) give
\[
 |\tau_1(z_0)-\tau_0(z_0)|
 =\pi_1ah_T^\lambda
 \asymp\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right\}^{\lambda/d}.  \tag{7}
\]
This proves the required geometric-mixing common-submeasure certificate.

Fix \(s,z_0\) and
\(\xi\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\).  All probabilities below are
under \(\mathbb K_\xi\).  Since \(0<\lambda\le1\), \(r=0\), and the Gram
matrix is scalar.  Local positivity and continuity of \(K\) give
\(k_0>0\) and \(\eta\in(0,\delta_0]\) such that
\(K(v)\ge k_0\) when \(\|v\|_2\le\eta\).  The ball
\(B(z_{0s},\eta b)\) lies in the cube, and the conditional density lower
bound gives, uniformly in \(t\),
\[
 p_{tb}:=\Pr\{\|X_{st}-z_{0s}\|_2\le\eta b\}
 \ge c_Xv_d\eta^db^d=:c_pb^d.                               \tag{1}
\]
If \(M_b\) counts these visits, then
\[
 G_{sT}(z_{0s},b)\ge\frac{k_0M_b}{Tb^d}.                    \tag{2}
\]

Set
\[
 a_T=\left\lceil\frac{3\log(T\vee2)}{|\log\rho_0|}\right\rceil.
\]
Partition the dates into consecutive blocks of length \(a_T\), and for each
parity retain alternate complete blocks.  Retained blocks are separated by
a complete block.  Iterative beta-mixing coupling bounds, for each parity,
the total variation distance between the retained-block law and the product
of its block marginals by
\[
 \left\lceil\frac{T}{a_T}\right\rceil\beta_0\rho_0^{a_T}
 \le CT^{-2}.                                                 \tag{3}
\]
This comparison concerns only the design and uses no response-calendar
independence.

For one independent comparison block let \(Y_j\in[0,a_T]\) count its
visits.  Convexity puts \(e^{-y/a_T}\) below the chord joining its endpoint
values, so (1) gives
\[
 \mathbb Ee^{-Y_j/a_T}
 \le1-\frac{1-e^{-1}}{a_T}\mathbb EY_j
 \le\exp(-cb^d).                                             \tag{4}
\]
Exponential Markov under the product-block law, followed by (3) for the two
parities, yields constants \(c_1,C_1>0\) such that
\[
 \Pr\{M_b\le c_1Tb^d\}
 \le C_1\exp(-c_1Tb^d/a_T)+C_1T^{-2}                         \tag{5}
\]
whenever \(Tb^d\ge C_1a_T\); after enlarging \(C_1\), the inequality is
trivial below that scale.  The stated compatibility of \(c_G\), together
with (2), makes the Gram at least \(c_G\) off the event in (5).

Put
\[
 b_\circ=(Tn_s)^{-1/(2\lambda+d)}\vee N^{-1/2}
          \vee(a_T/T)^{1/d}.                                 \tag{6}
\]
The least dyadic grid point not below a number is at most twice that number.
Apply (5) at dyadic candidates of order \(2^jb_\circ\).  Couple the entire
finite family of bad-scale events once before applying the product-law union
bound, so the comparison error \(CT^{-2}\) is charged only once.  Exponential
tail summation gives
\[
 \Pr\{h_s^\star>C2^jb_\circ\}
 \le C\exp(-c2^{jd})+CT^{-2}                                 \tag{7}
\]
until the scale reaches one, and hence
\[
 \mathbb E(h_s^\star)^{2\lambda}
 \le Cb_\circ^{2\lambda}+CT^{-2}.                            \tag{8}
\]
When \(b_\circ\) is bounded away from zero, (8) follows directly from
\(h_s^\star\le1\).  Since \(a_T\le C\log(T\vee2)\) and
\(2\lambda/d\le2\), (6)--(8) imply
\[
 \mathbb E(h_s^\star)^{2\lambda}
 \le C\left\{(Tn_s)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}+N^{-\lambda}
 +\left(\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right)^{2\lambda/d}\right\}. \tag{9}
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz proves the asserted bound for
\(\mathbb E(h_s^\star)^\lambda\).

At \(b=1\), (1)--(5) give
\(\Pr\{G_{sT}(z_{0s},1)<c_G\}\le CT^{-2}\).  If this fails for no cohort,
then \((z_{0s},1)\) belongs to every fold--cohort anchor set and fallback is
impossible.  A union bound over fixed \(S\) proves
\[
 \sup_{\xi\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)}
 \Pr_{\mathbb K_\xi}(\mathsf F_{\mathrm{fb}})\le CT^{-2}.   \tag{10}
\]
All constants are uniform because the fixed-query density and mixing bounds
are uniform.  On \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm{iid}}_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\), take
\(a_T=1\) and omit (3), replacing the final term in (9) by
\(T^{-2\lambda/d}\).  Finally the corrected transfer lemma supplies the
labelled point \(\xi_P(z_0)\) for marginal-almost-every admissible query of
each panel law, so these kernel conclusions transfer exactly on that conull
set.

Fix \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\) and a regular conditional law
\(\mathbb K_{P,z_0}=P(\,\cdot\mid z_0)\).  Define
\[
 \mu_{P,s}(z_0)=\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0],
 \qquad
 \Sigma_P(z_0)=\operatorname{Var}_P(Z_j\mid z_0),            \tag{1}
\]
and retain \(m=(m_1,\ldots,m_S)\).  Bounded wealth makes the first quantity
finite.  Assumption \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering} says that its
value is common across replicas \(i\), and it gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_{P,z_0}}B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}
 =\mu_{P,s}(z_0).                                             \tag{2}
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:consistency} disintegrates to
\(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}=B_{si}(1)\) almost surely under the kernel, and
\texttt{ass:event-date-transport} gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_{P,z_0}}B_{si}(0)=m_s(z_{0s}).         \tag{3}
\]
Thus (2)--(3) verify the common mean label, consistency, and transport
clauses of \texttt{def:fixed-query-kernel-class}.

Let \(\mathcal X=\sigma((X_{uv})_{u,v})\).  The two conditional-mean
equalities in \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering} become, under the
regular conditional law,
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_{P,z_0}}[Q_{sti}\mid\mathcal X]
 =m_s(X_{st}),
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_{P,z_0}}
 [B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathcal X]
 =\mu_{P,s}(z_0).                                             \tag{4}
\]
These are mean restrictions only.  They impose neither identical replica
distributions nor independence between training and event coordinates of a
unit history.  Assumption \texttt{ass:cross-unit-independence} becomes
conditional independence of the histories across \((s,i)\) given
\(\mathcal X\) under \(\mathbb K_{P,z_0}\).

The boundedness, exact-observation, and interior assertions disintegrate to
kernel-almost-sure assertions outside a marginally null set.  Holder
membership is a property of the retained labels.  Assumptions
\texttt{ass:design-density} and \texttt{ass:temporal-mixing} give, on a
marginally conull set,
\[
 c_X\le f_{st\mid z_0}(x)\le C_X
 \quad\text{for Lebesgue-almost every \(x\)},
 \qquad
 \beta_s(k\mid z_0)\le\beta_0\rho_0^k                       \tag{5}
\]
for every \(s,t\) and every integer \(k\ge1\).

Assumptions \texttt{ass:donor-independence} and
\texttt{ass:donor-training-separation} give, under the kernel, i.i.d. donors
independent of the complete joint panel.  Donor unbiasedness, ellipticity,
the fourth-moment condition, and (1) give
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_{P,z_0}}Z_j=z_0,
 \qquad c_\Sigma I_{Sd}\preceq\Sigma_P(z_0)\preceq C_\Sigma I_{Sd}, \tag{6}
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_{P,z_0}}
 \|\Sigma_P(z_0)^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)\|_2^4\le B^4.              \tag{7}
\]
The lower eigenvalue \(c_\Sigma>0\) makes the inverse square root in (7)
well defined.

There are finitely many cohorts, dates, and replicas, and countably many
lags.  Intersecting the conull query sets supporting (2)--(7) and the
disintegrated support assertions therefore leaves a marginally conull set.
At every query in it, the labelled tuple
\[
 \xi_P(z_0)=\bigl(\mathbb K_{P,z_0};\mu_P(z_0),m,
                         \Sigma_P(z_0)\bigr)                 \tag{8}
\]
satisfies every member property in
\texttt{def:fixed-query-kernel-class}; hence
\(\xi_P(z_0)\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\).  Equation (8), not the
bare law \(\mathbb K_{P,z_0}\), is the well-typed class member.  Nothing is
asserted about an arbitrarily selected conditional version on the
complementary null set.

Write
\[
 \rho_s=\rho_{sX}(z_{0s}),\qquad
 D_X=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\rho_s^\lambda,\qquad
 A=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}.                       \tag{1}
\]
For a feasible \((f,g,z)\) in
\texttt{def:joint-product-modulus}, put \(q_s=f_s-g_s\) and let \(t_s\)
be a nearest design index to \(z_{0s}\).  Nonnegativity of the response
budget implies
\[
 |q_s(X_{st_s})|^2\le\sum_{t=1}^{T}|q_s(X_{st})|^2\le n_s^{-1}. \tag{2}
\]
The difference of two functions in \(\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\) is
\(\lambda\)-Holder with constant at most \(2L\); hence
\[
 |q_s(z_{0s})|\le n_s^{-1/2}+2L\rho_s^\lambda.              \tag{3}
\]
The donor budget and \(\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I_{Sd}\) give
\[
 \|z-z_0\|_2\le C_\Sigma^{1/2}
       \|\Sigma^{-1/2}(z-z_0)\|_2
 \le C_\Sigma^{1/2}N^{-1/2}.                               \tag{4}
\]
Splitting at \(g_s(z_{0s})\), using Holder continuity,
\(\sum_s\pi_s=1\), and
\(\sum_s\pi_sn_s^{-1/2}\le S^{1/2}A^{1/2}\), yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 |\mathcal T(f,z_0)-\mathcal T(g,z)|
 &\le\sum_s\pi_s|q_s(z_{0s})|
      +L\sum_s\pi_s\|z_s-z_{0s}\|_2^\lambda\\
 &\le C\{A^{1/2}+D_X+N^{-\lambda/2}\}.
 \end{aligned}                                               \tag{5}
\]
Taking the supremum proves the upper bound for \(\Omega_X\).  The same
argument for one cohort and no donor displacement proves the stated upper
bound for \(\omega_{s,X}\).

For the fixed-design lower bounds let
\(\mathcal X_s=\{X_{s1},\ldots,X_{sT}\}\) and
\[
 q_s(x)=a\operatorname{dist}(x,\mathcal X_s)^\lambda,        \tag{6}
\]
where \(a>0\) is small enough in terms of \(B,L,d\).  Distance to a
nonempty closed set is one-Lipschitz, and subadditivity for
\(0<\lambda\le1\) gives
\[
 |u^\lambda-v^\lambda|\le|u-v|^\lambda\quad(u,v\ge0).       \tag{7}
\]
Thus \(f_s=q_s/2\) and \(g_s=-q_s/2\) lie in
\(\mathcal F_{\lambda,L,B}\), agree at every design site, and differ at
\(z_{0s}\) by \(a\rho_s^\lambda\).  Taking \(z=z_0\), first in one
cohort and then simultaneously in all cohorts, gives
\[
 \omega_{s,X}(1;z_{0s})\ge a\rho_s^\lambda,
 \qquad \Omega_X(1;z_0,\Sigma)\ge aD_X.                    \tag{8}
\]

Suppose \(\delta_0<1/2\).  Choose a signed coordinate vector \(v\) pointing
toward \(1/2\), and choose
\(a_0\le\tfrac12\min\{c_\Sigma^{1/2},1/2-\delta_0\}\).
Then \(u_N=a_0N^{-1/2}v\) keeps \(z_0+u_N\) in the trimmed cube and
\[
 N\|\Sigma^{-1/2}u_N\|_2^2
 \le Nc_\Sigma^{-1}\|u_N\|_2^2\le1.                       \tag{9}
\]
In the affected cohort a sufficiently small multiple of
\(x\mapsto\{v_s^\top(x-z_{0s})\}_+^\lambda\) belongs to
\(\mathcal F_{\lambda,L,B}\).  Use it as both \(f_s\) and \(g_s\), use
zero surfaces elsewhere, and take \(z=z_0+u_N\).  The response budget is
zero and the functional separation is at least \(cN^{-\lambda/2}\), because
the affected cohort has positive fixed weight.  Therefore
\[
 \Omega_X(1;z_0,\Sigma)\ge cN^{-\lambda/2}.                 \tag{10}
\]
Equations (5), (8), and (10), with
\(R_{X,\mathrm{opt}}=A\vee\Omega_X(1;z_0,\Sigma)^2\), prove
\[
 R_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\asymp A\vee D_X^2\vee N^{-\lambda}.    \tag{11}
\]
Without strict slack, (5) still proves the asserted upper characterization.

Finally suppose \(g_{sT}(z_0)<1\) for every \(s\).  Since
\(0<\lambda\le1\), the order convention gives \(r=0\), so the Gram is
scalar.  Its strict positivity at \((z_{0s},h_s^\star)\), together with the
support of \(K\), implies \(\rho_s\le h_s^\star\).  The bandwidth floor
implies
\[
 \{Tn_s(h_s^\star)^d\}^{-1/2}\le(h_s^\star)^\lambda.       \tag{12}
\]
Substituting \(D_X\le\sum_s\pi_s(h_s^\star)^\lambda\) and (12) into the
upper characterization and Definition \texttt{def:conditional-rate} gives
\(R_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\le CR_D\).  No lower local-modulus condition was used.

Put \(q=Sd\).  Choose a signed coordinate vector \(e\) pointing toward
\(1/2\) and set
\[
 w=\frac{\Sigma^{-1/2}e}{\|\Sigma^{-1/2}e\|_2}.
\]
Let \(O\) be orthogonal with first column \(w\).  Since \(B^4>q^2\), choose
\(\epsilon\in(0,B^4-q^2)\), put \(a=(1+\epsilon)^{1/2}>1\), and, for
\(|u|\) small, define \(A_u\in\{-a,0,a\}\) by
\[
 p_+(u)=\frac{1+u^2}{2a^2}+\frac{u}{2a},\quad
 p_-(u)=\frac{1+u^2}{2a^2}-\frac{u}{2a},\quad
 p_0(u)=1-\frac{1+u^2}{a^2}.                                \tag{1}
\]
All three probabilities are positive near zero, and direct summation gives
\[
 \mathbb EA_u=u,\qquad \mathbb EA_u^2=1+u^2,
 \qquad\operatorname{Var}(A_u)=1.                           \tag{2}
\]
Let \(R_2,\ldots,R_q\) be independent Rademacher variables, independent of
\(A_u\), and set \(V_u=O(A_u,R_2,\ldots,R_q)^\top\).  Then
\[
 \mathbb EV_u=uw,\qquad\operatorname{Var}(V_u)=I_q,          \tag{3}
\]
and orthogonal invariance gives
\[
 \mathbb E\|V_u-uw\|_2^4
 =\mathbb E(A_u-u)^4+2(q-1)+(q-1)^2.                        \tag{4}
\]
At zero the right side is
\(a^2+2(q-1)+(q-1)^2=q^2+\epsilon<B^4\).  It is continuous in \(u\), so
it remains at most \(B^4\) after shrinking the neighborhood.

Let \(G_u\) be the law of \(Z_u=z_0+\Sigma^{1/2}V_u\).  Equations (3)--(4)
give
\[
 z(u):=\mathbb EZ_u
 =z_0+\frac{u}{\|\Sigma^{-1/2}e\|_2}e,\qquad
 \operatorname{Var}(Z_u)=\Sigma,                            \tag{5}
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb E\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_u-z(u))\|_2^4\le B^4.          \tag{6}
\]
The Hellinger affinity between \(G_0\) and \(G_u\) is
\(a_H(u)=\sum_{r\in\{-,0,+\}}\{p_r(0)p_r(u)\}^{1/2}\).
The probabilities in (1) stay bounded away from zero near zero, so
\(a_H''\) is bounded there; also \(a_H(0)=1\) and
\(a_H'(0)=\tfrac12\sum_rp_r'(0)=0\).  Taylor's formula therefore gives
\[
 a_H(u)\ge1-Cu^2.                                            \tag{7}
\]
For \(CNu^2\le1/2\), product factorization and
\(1-x\ge e^{-2x}\) give \(a_H(u)^N\ge e^{-2CNu^2}\).  For dominated
laws, Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \|P-G\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le\left\{1-\left(\int\sqrt{dP\,dG}\right)^2\right\}^{1/2}. \tag{8}
\]
Choose \(c_\eta>0\) small enough that (7)--(8), with
\(u=c_\eta N^{-1/2}\), make the product total variation at most
\(1-\eta\).  Reduce \(c_\eta\) so it is in the moment neighborhood and
\(c_\eta C_\Sigma^{1/2}\le1/2-\delta_0\).  Equation (5) then yields
\[
 N\|\Sigma^{-1/2}\{z(u)-z_0\}\|_2^2=c_\eta^2.              \tag{9}
\]
Moreover \(\|\Sigma^{-1/2}e\|_2^{-1}\le C_\Sigma^{1/2}\); hence the
one-coordinate displacement toward \(1/2\) preserves the interior
restriction.  Taking \(G_0=G_{u=0}\) and
\(G_1=G_{u=c_\eta N^{-1/2}}\) proves every assertion.

 \qquad

\]
and retain the regression label \(m=(m_1,\ldots,m_S)\).  Then, for

proposed.consumer: All fixed-query risk, coverage, and model-audit conclusions use this labelled point when transferring back to the panel class.

proposed_core_edits.proposed: At a fixed admissible query \(z_0\), consistency, cohort-common treated-mean replication, and event-date transport identify \(\tau(z_0)=\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{\mu_s-m_s(z_{0s})\}\) for every labelled point \(\xi\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\). For \(0<\lambda\le1\), the deterministic experiment \(\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)\) treats \(X,z_0,\Sigma\) as known specifications and permits a rule depending on them, selected before only the unknown label. In contrast, every outer random-design MSE or interval rule is one \(\mathcal O\)-measurable rule selected before the unknown donor mean \(z_0\) and labelled kernel; this is the convention under which the \(N^{-\lambda}\) donor phase is nondegenerate. The marginal squared-risk scale is \(R_\star=R_{\mathrm{or}}\vee N^{-\lambda}\), with the independent-calendar spacing replacement on \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm{iid}}_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\). The feasible interval uses whole-unit concentration and no calendar-score branch. For every joint panel law, the repaired transfer lemma constructs the labelled point \(\xi_P(z_0)=(\mathbb K_{P,z_0};\mu_P(z_0),m,\Sigma_P(z_0))\) and places that tuple, rather than the bare regular conditional kernel, in the fixed-query class for marginal-almost-every query. Only there do causal risk and coverage conclusions transfer. No supremum is taken over panel-specific null conditional values, no lower local modulus is assumed, and no headline result is claimed for \(\lambda>1\).
proposed_core_edits.reason: The former metadata described a labelled conditional kernel as if it were itself the class member; the repaired metadata names the labelled tuple and preserves the estimand and every rate.

prose_updates.tldr: The paper delivers the rough-Holder frontier for \(0<\lambda\le1\). A repaired sampling condition makes each cohort's treated conditional mean common across replicas while leaving their distributions and within-unit training/event dependence unrestricted. The deterministic fixed-design experiment treats \(X,z_0,\Sigma\) as known specifications, whereas every outer generated-query estimator and interval is one observable rule chosen before the unknown donor mean; this distinction preserves the \(N^{-\lambda}\) phase. At each admissible query, uniform random-design statements are over \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\). For a panel law, the bridge constructs the labelled point \(\xi_P(z_0)=(\mathbb K_{P,z_0};\mu_P(z_0),m,\Sigma_P(z_0))\) and places that tuple, not the bare conditional kernel, in the fixed-query class only for marginal-almost-every query. The nonredundant channels are treated replication, query-conditional calendar spacing, and full-covariance donor location; the feasible interval concentrates whole unit histories and has no calendar-score branch.

project_justification.gap: Classical fixed-point regression does not combine replicated sites with an external full-covariance generated query, and the former panel-to-kernel wording applied membership in a labelled class to a bare conditional probability law. A panel regular conditional law is also not defined canonically at query-null values.
project_justification.niche: Historical paths are observed exactly while only the event query is synthesized. The common-mean condition closes the treated-replica transfer without imposing identical distributions, within-unit training/event independence, or response-calendar mixing. The bridge keeps the kernel component \(\mathbb K_{P,z_0}\) distinct from the labelled class member \(\xi_P(z_0)\), and known-specification recovery remains distinct from unknown-query outer decision theory.
project_justification.fill: The note proves conditional, marginal, and honest-length rate frontiers for \(0<\lambda\le1\). A nearest-site rule attains the deterministic fixed-design scale when \(X,z_0,\Sigma\) are known specifications; an anchor/extrapolation rule and total interval remain single observable procedures chosen before the unknown donor mean. Explicit treated, spacing, and full-covariance donor pairs match the upper rates. For every panel law, the tuple \(\xi_P(z_0)=(\mathbb K_{P,z_0};\mu_P(z_0),m,\Sigma_P(z_0))\) supplies the well-typed causal bridge for marginal-almost-every query.

sampling_model.design: At a fixed admissible query, each exact-design coordinate has conditional density between \(c_X\) and \(C_X\) almost everywhere and each cohort's design sequence is geometrically beta mixing. The independent-calendar subclass imposes conditional independence only on design dates. From a panel law these clauses are inherited by the labelled point \(\xi_P(z_0)\) only on a marginal-conull set of queries.
sampling_model.units: Each cohort supplies \(n_s\) replicated untreated blocks and \(n_s\) treated event outcomes. Conditional on the exact design, unit histories are independent across replicas. Their training responses have mean \(m_s(X_{st})\), and every treated replica has the same cohort mean \(\mu_s(z_0)\), invariant under further design conditioning. Full distributions may differ across replicas, and dependence across training dates and the event within one unit remains unrestricted.
sampling_model.treatment: Consistency identifies observed event wealth with treated potential wealth. The repaired replication clause makes its conditional mean common within cohort. Event-date transport separately equates the unobserved untreated event mean with the historical regression at the realized path; neither centering nor query overlap proves that causal equality.
sampling_model.overlap: Every admitted query is at least \(\delta_0\) from the cube boundary. The donor-location converse uses strict slack \(\delta_0<1/2\); exact fixed-design recovery can be easier when a design site equals the query.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Only the event query is generated. Donor folds provide projected means and the full stacked covariance retains all cross-coordinate, cross-horizon, and cross-cohort entries. For \(0<\lambda\le1\), local-constant weights are nonnegative and have unit mass, so whole-unit bounded-range concentration suffices without response mixing, deconvolution, or calendar-score studentization.

prose_updates.related_work: Donoho (1994) studies a known Gaussian convex experiment; here the deterministic bounded product experiment instead has replicated responses, an external full-covariance location coordinate, and fixed specifications \(X,z_0,\Sigma\) known to its decision rule. Akhavan, Gogolashvili, and Tsybakov (2024) study independently estimated minimizers under strong convexity, where center error is second order rather than a rough-Holder modulus. Armstrong and Kolesar (2018, 2020) provide ordered-modulus and bias-aware ordinary-regression interval benchmarks, while Cattaneo, Feng, and Titiunik (2021) study dependent synthetic-control prediction; none supplies an outer generated-query rule, the labelled panel-to-fixed-query tuple \(\xi_P(z_0)\), or the donor expected-length converse proved here. Stone (1982), Fan (1993), Mammen, Rothe, and Schienle (2012), Delaigle, Hall, and Meister (2008), Low (1997), and Ferman (2021) remain rate, generated-covariate, adaptation, and replication context rather than substitutes for the theorem.
prose_updates.interpretation: The fixed-query class consists of labelled points, not probability kernels alone. For a panel law, \(\mathbb K_{P,z_0}\) is only the kernel component of \(\xi_P(z_0)=(\mathbb K_{P,z_0};\mu_P(z_0),m,\Sigma_P(z_0))\), and the transfer theorem asserts membership of this tuple for marginal-almost-every query. Its common treated mean is a mean restriction only: it does not homogenize replica distributions or break dependence within a unit history. Donor uncertainty dominates when \(N^{-\lambda}\) exceeds treated replication and conditional spacing. A deterministic optimal-recovery rule may use known \(X,z_0,\Sigma\); the outer feasible rule may not use \(z_0\), because it must learn that donor mean.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Every constructive headline is restricted to \(0<\lambda\le1\) and fixed admissible queries; panel-law statements are obtained through the labelled point \(\xi_P(z_0)\) only marginal-almost-everywhere in the query. The common treated-mean restriction is necessary for the present deterministic-experiment transfer but does not control conditional variances or higher moments beyond boundedness. For \(\lambda>1\), signed local-polynomial weights need additional stochastic stability. Geometric conditional design mixing retains the logarithmic spacing penalty, the donor converse requires \(B^4>(Sd)^2\) and \(\delta_0<1/2\), and exact phase-intersection constants remain open.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Event-date transport remains untestable. The centering condition imposes a common treated conditional mean across replicas and invariance to the exact design, but no identical distributions, within-unit training/event independence, or response-calendar mixing. Fixed-design minimax rules know \(X,z_0,\Sigma\); outer risk and interval rules are chosen before the unknown \(z_0\) and label. The interval uses no calendar-score branch or estimated-variance division. The panel bridge places the labelled tuple \(\xi_P(z_0)\), rather than its bare regular conditional kernel, in the fixed-query class only on a marginal-conull query set. Higher smoothness, growing dimension, adaptation, uniform-in-query bands, and exact constants remain outside scope.
